_comment: The shipped provider catalogue. DATA, not code — adding a provider is an
edit here, never a rebuild.
WHY THIS IS FIVE ENTRIES AND NOT 346.
It briefly held 346, ported out of the OmniRoute source: their catalogue
transformed into Primnox's schema. That was the wrong thing to build. Only
103 of the 346 carried an endpoint Primnox could actually call — the rest
live in a package OmniRoute publishes rather than in its source — and
keeping the other 243 current would have meant tracking someone else's
release cycle by hand, forever, to remain a worse copy of it.
OmniRoute already solves this, properly, as its whole job. So Primnox
points AT OmniRoute instead of impersonating it: one endpoint, and the
290-odd providers behind it stay OmniRoute's to maintain. Choosing among
them happens in OmniRoute's own dashboard, which is the surface built for
it and the one that will still be right next month.
What remains here is the shape of the decision Primnox still owns: route
through the gateway, or run entirely on this machine.
`kind` selects the discovery strategy AND the trust class:
ollama   — asks /api/tags natively; on-device, never scrubbed
local    — OpenAI-compatible on this machine; on-device, never scrubbed
cloud    — someone else's server; scrubbed at the gate
gateway  — LISTENS on localhost, FORWARDS to the cloud. Scrubbed like
cloud, because the address is not the destination. This is
the one that matters most now: every hosted turn Primnox
makes goes through a gateway on 127.0.0.1, so if that ever
reads as `local` the Privacy Mirror stops applying to all
of it at once.
A user file at <data root>/providers.json overrides and extends this one
by name, so a direct endpoint or a private gateway survives an update.

providers.name: OmniRoute
providers.hint: Primnox's default route to every hosted model. It runs on this machine and forwards to whichever provider it picks, so it needs no key here — credentials live in OmniRoute, not in Primnox. Pick a routing channel rather than a named model: a channel keeps the fallback that is the reason to run it.

providers.name: Ollama (local)
providers.hint: Models running on your own hardware. No key, no account, no network — and the only configuration where nothing you type leaves the machine at all.

providers.name: LM Studio (local)
providers.hint: LM Studio's local server. Start it from LM Studio's Developer tab; the default port is 1234.

providers.name: llama.cpp (local)
providers.hint: A llama-server instance on this machine. The default port is 8080.

providers.name: Direct endpoint
providers.hint: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, called directly rather than through the gateway. For a private deployment, a company proxy, or a provider you would rather Primnox reach without OmniRoute in between.
